pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values - Coombe Boys’ School
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Coombe Boys’ School, is a community of learners that embraces innovation and inclusivity in teaching, leading to academic excellence and a world of opportunity for all.
We strive to foster a culture of creativity and critical thinking that empowers our students to become confident lifelong learners and responsible global citizens. Our commitment to providing a diverse and inclusive learning environment ensures that every student is heard, recognised as an individual and feels valued and respected.
Our focus on academic excellence prepares them for success in an ever changing world. Our goal is to inspire our students to think beyond the classroom and to explore the endless possibilities that lie ahead, so that they may confidently shape their own futures and make a positive impact on the world.
Coombe prepares each student for their World of Opportunity by:
As part of Helix Learning Trust, we continue to build on the strong foundations, expertise and relationships developed through the Coombe Academy Trust, while benefiting from being part of a diverse family of mainstream and specialist schools. Working collaboratively across the Trust enables us to share expertise, resources and best practice, while retaining our individual school identity, ethos and commitment to our pupils and communities.
Our vision, “Preparing our communities for a future of possibility,” remains at the heart of everything we do. As the Trust has grown, this vision continues to guide our ambition for our staff, pupils, schools and wider communities.
For our staff, this means supporting successful and fulfilling careers throughout their time with the Trust. For our pupils, it means developing the knowledge, skills and independence they need to be successful throughout their education and beyond. For our schools, it means creating the conditions in which they can flourish, and for our wider communities, it means recognising and valuing the power of collaboration with the Trust.
Find out more about the Ethos, Values and Curriculum Principles of the Helix Learning Trust

Headteacher's Welcome
Here at Coombe Boys’ School our values of Excellence, Ambition and Integrity are the foundations of all that we seek to achieve for every student.
We believe that every pupil deserves the best possible education to help them reach their full potential, and we're proud to be experts in providing just that.
Our commitment to excellence means that we strive to create a supportive and inspiring environment where students can learn, grow, and succeed both academically and personally. With our unwavering ambition, we encourage our students to aim high and never give up on their goals.
With our expectation of integrity, we foster a culture of honesty, respect, and accountability that permeates everything we do. So if you're looking for a school that can help your son become the best version of himself, you've come to the right place!
We believe it is essential that school is a challenging, inspirational and transformational experience. We also believe that it must provide a moral framework for learners to live their lives by and that students perform their best when they feel supported, confident and happy.
We aim to develop a passion in every student and our extensive enrichment provision; extra-curricular programme and wide range of trips and activities, ensures that students discover what their passion is and they are provided with the support and provision to pursue this.
We are enormously proud of our academic, sporting and cultural successes, however it is the fact that parents tell us that their sons are happy here and that they enjoy coming to school that we are most proud of. I am confident that if you choose to send your son to Coombe then they too will experience a World of Opportunity.
David Smith Headteacher

Exam Results and School Performance
August 2026
Excellence at Every Level: Record GCSE Attainment for Coombe Boys’ Students
Our Year 11 Class of 2026 are celebrating another excellent year of GCSE results, with pupils across the full range of abilities achieving the best attainment outcomes in the school’s history.
This year’s results represent a significant milestone for the school, with higher, middle and lower prior-attaining learners all achieving their strongest-ever results. The excellent outcomes demonstrate the progress and success of students across the whole school community, ensuring that every young person has the opportunity to achieve and move confidently on to their next stage of education.
The results reflect the hard work, ambition and determination of our Year 11 boys, alongside the dedication of staff and the invaluable support of parents and families.
The school is particularly proud that this success has been achieved across all ability groups. From students securing the very highest grades to those making outstanding progress from their individual starting points, this year’s results demonstrate that high expectations, excellent teaching and the right support can enable every student to succeed.
Mr Smith, Headteacher, said:
“We are incredibly proud of our Year 11 students. These results are not only a celebration of individual achievement, but a landmark moment for the school. Students across our higher, middle and lower prior-attaining groups have achieved the best results in our history.
What makes these outcomes particularly special is that this is success for all. Our students have shown what can be achieved through hard work, resilience and ambition, and we are delighted to see so many young people rewarded for their efforts.
I would like to thank our staff, parents and families for the support they have provided throughout the students’ time at Coombe. Most importantly, I want to congratulate our Year 11 students and wish them every success as they take their next steps.”
For many students, these results mark the next step in their journey as they progress to Coombe Sixth Form, where they will continue to build on their achievements and prepare for the exciting opportunities that lie ahead.
These outcomes are a powerful reflection of our ongoing commitment to Excellence, Ambition and Integrity, and our determination to ensure that students of every starting point are supported and challenged to fulfil their potential.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026.
Result Summary 2025
August 2025
Bright Futures Ahead as the Coombe Boys' Class of 2025 celebrates GCSE Results Success
Coombe Boys' School is proud to announce another year of excellent GCSE results, continuing its tradition of year-on-year improvement and demonstrating the school’s ongoing commitment to preparing students for a world of opportunity.
This year’s results reflect the hard work, dedication, and resilience of the students, as well as the ongoing support and guidance of staff and families. With these achievements as a strong foundation, students are now set to take their next steps with confidence, whether that is progressing to sixth form, embarking on apprenticeships, or pursuing other exciting educational and vocational pathways.
Mr Smith, Headteacher said:
“We are immensely proud of our students. Each year they continue to raise the bar, showing real determination and ambition. These results are not just about grades, they are about the skills, character, and confidence our boys are taking with them into the next stage of their education and beyond. Our students leave GCSEs ready to embrace challenges, seize opportunities, and shape their futures. This continuous progress year-on-year is a testament to their hard work and the dedication of everyone at Coombe Boys’ School.”
The school celebrates the sustained improvement over recent years, highlighting the impact of focused teaching, tailored support, and the students’ own perseverance. This year’s students have excelled across a wide range of subjects, with exceptional outcomes in Maths, English, Triple Science, Drama, Business and Religious Studies to name a few.
With such strong foundations, students are now set to embark on a world of opportunities. The achievements are not seen as an end point but as the beginning of bright futures.
Students next steps include:
The school would also like to take a moment to thank all staff, students, and their families for their outstanding work, ongoing support, and dedication throughout this time. We look forward to supporting the class of 2025 as they take their next steps.
Result Summary 2024
August 2024
Congratulations to all Coombe Boys’ students receiving their GCSE, Vocational & Technical Qualification results today.
Today our Year 11 boys celebrate fantastic results with an outstanding 5.7% increase in students achieving Grades 9-7 the top grades awarded (A, A* & A**). The school has once again seen a 5% increase on last year’s results which remain significantly above the National average for boys in all areas and for all groups of learners and continues the sustained upward trend. Meanwhile many boys swept the board with straight 9-7 grades.
Among the top achievers are:
Mohammed Ellahi who has been awarded x10 Grade 9’s (A**).
Reuben Goddard who has been awarded x9 Grade 9’s (A**) and is going on to study A Level Mathematics, Chemistry, History and Physics at Coombe Sixth Form
Kayden Chu who has been awarded x7 Grade 9’s (A**) and x4 Grade 8’s.
Deputy Head Boy Omar Elamahroukey who has been awarded x6 Grade 9’s (A**) & x4 Grade 8’s.
Jason Feng who was awarded x8 Grade 9’s (A**).
Andrew Wong who was awarded x8 Grade 9’s (A**)
Other boys celebrating Grade 9’s (A**) alongside a string of Grade 8’s (A*) and Grade 7’s (A) include Stefan Suvei, Ollie Bodely-Scott, Tony Kim and James Tse.
As our boys take their next steps into further education we are of course delighted to see them enrolling into the Coombe Sixth Form today as they begin their final two years with us here at Coombe. We were pleased to be able to speak with many this morning whose success on GCSE, Vocational & Technical Level 2 pathways has prepared the way for their next steps.
Just some of the students enrolling this morning amongst many include;
Head Boy Joshua Pritchard-Chase who will be studying A Level History, English Language/Literature and Performing Arts
Joshua Davis who will be studying A Level Biology, Chemistry and Geography
Clarence Duke-Deshields who will be studying A Level Psychology, Film Studies and Performing Arts
Daniel O’Sullivan who will be studying A Level History, Psychology and Performing Arts
Tony Kim who will be studying A Level Mathematics, French and Biology
Monty Chappin who will be studying A Level Geography, History and English Literature
Mr David Smith, Headteacher of Coombe Boys’ School, said that
“We are very proud of our Year 11 boys. The class of 2024 have embraced the school's values of excellence, ambition and integrity, working hard alongside staff to be successful. I would like to take a moment to thank our staff, students and their families for their outstanding work, ongoing support and dedication during this time. It is also wonderful to see so many of our talented and highly-motivated boys in such a strong position to be successful in the next stage of their academic careers at the Coombe Sixth Form.”
Result Summary 2023
Congratulations to our GCSE and BTEC Level 2 students receiving their results today.
Today we are celebrating the achievements of our 2023 Year 11 students who have received their GCSE and BTEC Level 2 results. We are so proud of the resilience and determination this cohort has shown throughout their time at Coombe Boys’ School. They have had to face the challenging circumstances of the pandemic which led to their early years here being significantly disrupted, but they have emerged stronger for it. Our congratulations go out to each and every one of them.
Today’s results will be the stepping stones from which our students can take their next steps into further education, and we are delighted to see the majority of our boys enrolling at Coombe Sixth Form. We wish them every success on their A Level and BTEC Level 3 pathways which will no doubt lead them on to some exceptional university degree courses, apprenticeships and job opportunities.
It has been exciting to hear of students' plans today, and with such a wide choice of courses at Coombe Sixth Form they are certainly diverse. Examples of just some of our students celebrating this morning amongst many include:
Aidan Catchpool who will be studying A Level Maths, Further Maths and Computer Science
Joshua Barrett who will be studying Physics, Maths and Biology
Tyrone Reid who will be studying A Level English Literature & Language, Drama, Politics and Business Studies
Lachlan Anderson who will be studying A Level Maths, Further Maths, Computer Science and Physics
Rohan Cranfield who will be studying A Level Economics, Physics, Maths and Further Maths
Elliot James who will be studying A Level Psychology, Economics and Biology
Alfie Armstrong who will be studying A Level Computer Science, Maths and Physics
Headteacher Mr Smith, expressed his pride in the achievements of the students and the resilience they have demonstrated. He stated, "These results are a reflection of the hard work, determination, and adaptability of our students. We are immensely proud of their achievements and the progress they have made despite the early disruptions caused by the pandemic. I also extend my gratitude to our dedicated teaching staff for their unwavering support and commitment to our students' success."
Coombe Boys' School is committed to providing an exceptional learning experience for all its students, fostering their personal growth, and preparing them for the challenges of the future. For our students receiving results today, congratulations from everyone here at school.
If you would like to hear more about our students successes and their Coombe journeys, then take a look at our social media platforms and follow us on facebook @CoombeBoysSchool, instagram @coombeboysschool, and twitter @coombeboysnews.
Result Summary 2022
We are extremely proud of our 2022 Year 11 students who today are celebrating their achievements after an unprecedented two years. Their GCSE & BTEC achievements have been based on a positive, resilient and determined approach to their GCSE studies.
As our boys take their next steps into further education we are of course delighted to see our boys enrolling into the Coombe Sixth Form today becoming our new Year 12 cohort as they begin their final two years with us here at Coombe. We were pleased to be able to speak with many this morning whose success on GCSE and BTEC Level 2 pathways has prepared the way for their next steps.
The cohort achieved a Progress 8 score of +0.21 and an Attainment 8 score of 51. 69% achieved a grade 4 or above in English and Mathematics.
At Level 3 BTEC students achieved a progress score of +0.32 with the average grade of a Distinction.
Just some of the students celebrating this morning amongst many include:
It is fantastic to hear them chat excitedly about their grades and Level 3 subject choices from the wide range of 34 courses on offer spanning every area of the curriculum. It will be no time before they will be following in the footsteps of their Year 13 predecessors who are about to start on some exceptional university degree courses and apprenticeships.
Headteacher Mr Smith said
“We are very proud of our boys’ hard work and resilience. This is the first year that students have taken summer exams since 2019. It is therefore fantastic to see so many of our talented and highly-motivated boys in such a strong position to be successful in the next stage of their academic careers at the Coombe Sixth Form. I would like to take a moment to thank our staff, students and their families for their ongoing support and dedication during this time.”
Result Summary 2021
Congratulations to all Coombe students receiving their GCSE results today
Following a hugely successful A Level Results day where we were delighted to see so many of our boys attaining outstanding grades and securing places at their first choice Universities, we are also extremely proud of our 2021 Year 11 boys GCSE achievements, especially the way they have adapted to such a difficult and disrupted year.
This year, our congratulations to all our boys has a very particular significance given the resilience that they have all demonstrated in the face of 18 months of disruption to their learning, as well as uncertainty around the examination process. The excellent results that they have achieved therefore deserve the highest praise.
As our boys take the next steps of their Coombe Journey today, enrolling into the Coombe Sixth Form and becoming our new Year 12 cohort it is fantastic to hear them chat excitedly about their grades and Level 3 subject choices from the wide range of 34 courses on offer spanning every area of the curriculum. I am also immensely grateful to the team of dedicated staff and families for their ongoing support.”
We look forward to sharing our students' successes and their choices for the next stage of their Coombe journey across our social media platforms over the next few weeks.

pageCache.pageTitle: Specialist Resource Provision - Coombe Boys’ School
pageCache.text:
Specialist Resource Provision
Designation
Primary need is speech, language and communication (two years or more language delay/disorder). This includes boys with bilateral hearing loss (moderate to profound) with language delay or disorder; boys may also have a secondary need of social communication providing that their needs can be met in a lanuage rich environment and are compatible with the needs of children with hearing loss. Students will be able to access a differentiated mainstream curriculum.
How does it work?
Coombe Boys' SRP will have a cohort of 20 students when full. There will be four spaces per year group. All students come with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
What we offer
Students will be able to access a differentiated mainstream curriculum. The curriculum offered is bespoke to students' needs but generally students will access a combination of lessons in the SRP and in the mainstream.
Provision may include
Small-group specialist teaching for language-heavy subjects
Total Communication approach
Occupational therapy
Speech and language intervention
Interventions are built in
Use of Colourful Semantics and Shape Coding
Daily listening checks for students with equipment
Movement breaks and Zones of Regulation embedded into lessons
Staffing
Specialist Language teachers in the SRP
Specialist subject teachers in the mainstream
SRP Learning Support Assistants
Visiting Speech and Language Therapists
Visiting Occupational Therapist
Visiting Educational Psychologist
Resident Teacher of the Deaf
Future Pathways
Follow a modified KS3 curriculum
Bespoke KS4 pathway which may include:
Business Studies (Enterprise)
Digital Information Technology BTEC
Food Preparation & Nutrition
Performing Arts BTEC

Pleae email [email protected] for more information and to arrange a visit.

Careers and IAG
At Coombe Boys' School, we aim to embed ambition and raise aspirations in all of our young people, so they have the very best life chances. Our careers programme plays an extremely important role in ensuring that pupils receive high-quality, impartial advice and guidance, to enable them to make informed choices about post-16 progression routes and future careers.
We have designed a comprehensive careers programme that will allow pupils to develop the essential skills to be successful in the world of work. Our careers programme is designed to provide as many interactions with post-16 providers and employers as possible. This includes teacher-led activities during form period, work experience in year 10 and through engagement with local employers and other professionals.
When designing the Careers programme, we have taken into consideration all of the Gatsby Benchmarks and the Baker Clause, to ensure quality of provision.
We have a dedicated careers website where you can find out lots more information about our exciting careers programme.

Key Stage 4 Options
The information on this page will help to guide you and your son through the decision making process, enabling your son to make informed subject choices about their curriculum for Year 10 and 11.
At Coombe Boys’ School we are extremely ambitious for our students and our Key Stage 4 curriculum matches this. It is broad and balanced and accessible to all students.
We have a wide variety of subjects that allow students to personalise their curriculum in a way that suits their interests and talents. Our curriculum is truly inclusive and we offer a wide range of GCSE courses alongside a range of technical and vocational qualifications.
When considering which subjects to choose, it is important that your son makes informed choices and chooses subjects that he enjoys, that he has an interest in and that will motivate him to be the best that he can be, giving him the drive and determination to be successful.

Safeguarding
The Safeguarding Lead at Coombe Boys' School is Mrs Morris who can be contacted via the school enquiries phone number or by email: [email protected]
Mrs Morris - Deputy Headteacher and Designated Safeguarding Lead

We also have a student friendly version of our safeguarding policy: Child Friendly Safeguarding Policy
Pastoral Care
For all things health and wellbeing, see our Health and Wellbeing Portal
Key Pastoral Points
The welfare of all pupils is of vital importance and monitored closely throughout the tutorial system which is well established at Coombe.
When they join the school, each boy is placed in one of six Houses: Oak, Elm, Willow, Beech, Chestnut and Cedar. He will stay in the same house throughout his time at Coombe. Registration is taken in this group by the Tutor who is responsible for the boys’ well-being. This tutor group helps the boys to know that they matter as individuals. When possible, we try to keep the same teacher with the same tutor group throughout a boy’s time at Coombe.
The Head of Year, Deputy Head of Year and Tutor have a personal knowledge of each boy and are on hand to provide help and guidance in all aspects of school life. They communicate with parents and with external welfare agencies which provide support for the home and the school.
If you have any concerns
If you have any concerns about your son’s well-being, you should discuss them with his tutor or the Head of Year ( 020 8949 1537 / [email protected]) or use the enquiries form in the contact section.
The Pastoral Team all monitor the pupils progress closely via Coombe Boys' PSHE, which is part of the curriculum, provides help, guidance and opportunities for them to develop academically, socially and individually. Any problems or queries may be discussed with your son’s Tutor or Head of Year in school, by appointment, by telephone on 020 8949 1537, or by email on [email protected]
The Head of Year can refer any learning, behavioural or medical problems to the Education Welfare Officer, the Educational Psychologist and the School Nurse, who visit regularly.

pageCache.text:
Clubs and Extra Curricular Activities
At Coombe, we provide a rich programme of enrichment and extra-curricular activities to complement our excellent curriculum.
Students have a choice to explore activities that stimulate and further develop their mental, physical and creative skills. We encourage all our students to take part in weekly clubs, maintain healthy habits, make new friends and stretch their minds. As such we offer over 50 clubs each term. All but two of them are FREE.
Details of our enrichment and extra-curricular timetable and DofE Awards can be found by clicking the links below.
Let us challenge your son’s talents, nurture his interests and inspire the discovery of new ones as he prepares himself for a world of opportunity.
